why:
phase-427 W4 -- the ours-only, storage-free publisher: `create_publisher_in<M>(const char* topic, const QoS&)` returns the publisher BY VALUE and latches `ok()=false` instead of throwing. It came off `ComponentNode::create_publisher`, and the reason it does not keep that name is a collision the merge would otherwise have manufactured. Upstream's `create_publisher<M>(const std::string&, ...)` returns a `shared_ptr` and throws; as overloads on the one merged type those differ only in SIGNATURE, which C++ resolves silently -- measured with gcc 13, `create_publisher<M>("chatter", rclcpp::QoS(10))` bound OURS with nothing but a note that ISO calls it ambiguous, so a ported file would have compiled and got a different type, lifetime and failure channel. (The integer-depth spelling `("chatter", 10)` binds UPSTREAM, because `int -> size_t` is a standard conversion; the work item predicted the opposite and the measurement corrected it.) The fix is a different NAME, not a cleverer signature -- RFC-0089's `_in` rule, third application in this campaign after the reordered C node initialiser and the clock-taking C timer verb. `tests/compile/one_node_type_ours_only_names.cpp` pins both the positive and the negative control.

phase-427 (the `_in_group` split) -- `_in` here means ours-only/storage-free and nothing else. The callback-group form is `cpp:Node::create_publisher_in_group`; a first parameter of `CallbackGroup` is what the longer suffix names.
